ledger.note: 468: the recovery attempts end; the Song north-east is Wei land. 'In fall 467, Yuchi again defeated Shen Youzhi, ending Emperor Ming's efforts at recapturing Xu and Yan Provinces'; Qing and Ji follow in spring 468.

479: Xiao Daocheng ends the Liu Song and founds the Qi. 'In 479, Xiao took the throne himself and declared himself Emperor of Qi, ending Liu Song'; infobox 'Disestablished: 31 May 479'. The Wen-to-Shun succession had been a run of coups and revolts; Houfei was assassinated in 477 and Xiao 'placed Emperor Shun on his throne'.

notes: Cliopatria rows: the Liu Song shapes (426-479) start six years late (420) and, for 426-450, still hold every city south of the Yellow River that the Wei took in 422-423 and 430-431, and all of Shandong and Xuzhou, which pages date to the Wei only in 466-468. The 451 shape (Shandong dropped) is therefore early by fifteen years for the north-east and right from 468; verdicts and new keyframes 420, 423, 430, 466 and 468 carry the repair. The Henan lands are drawn with the northern-wei dossier's disc specs (Luoyang 120 km, Xuchang 80, Jining 100, Zhengzhou 80, Anyang 80) because the pages name cities, not extents; 'Jining' is the Shandong city. NOT SETTLED: (1) the south (Lingnan, Jiaozhou, Sichuan, the Tuyuhun front from 439): the pages opened are silent, so the Cliopatria shape stands unverified; the Yi Province rising of 432 (Wen page) changed no border. (2) Lâm Ấp 446: the occupation is page-dated only at the start. (3) Emperor Wen of Liu Song's alliance with Xia and Houfei-era revolts: no territorial effect on the pages. (4) The 466 revolt of Liu Zixun ('Nearly the entire empire declared for Liu Zixun', Jing Province and Kuaiji Commandery) lasted under a year, so no rebel dossier. (5) Western Qin, Xia: the neighbours list has them 426-438 but no Song border event is on the pages. Page budget: five pages, then a sixth (Lâm Ấp) for the champa mirror. REPAIR (2026-10-19, after review): (1) the 420-422 shape is now the Western Jin 420 shape minus the corrected xia_418 shape, so the 350 Weibei-Longdong cells that the Xia held are no longer Song; the predecessor land and the founding event use the same spec. (2) The Qinling and upper Han strip south of 34 N (278 cells) is not Xia's on any page; it stays Song in 420-422 and is added to the Song corrections of 423-479 by continuity (confidence 1), which makes it overlap the Cliopatria Northern Wei 439 shape that the northern-wei dossier uses: a conflict for the northern-wei owner. (3) NOT CHANGED, disagreement: the review asks to centre Huatai on Hua County (about 114.52 E, 35.58 N) instead of the 80 km Anyang disc, together with northern-wei /ledger/11. The Dao Yanzhi page failed to load (url_not_found, twice), the Hua County page says only that the county is the southmost part of Anyang and does not mention Huatai, and the Taiwu page puts Huatai at 'modern Anyang'; with no page tying Huatai to the county seat or giving coordinates, the disc stays until the northern-wei owner and a readable page settle it, so that both sides of the 430-431 pair change together. (4) Lâm Ấp 446 withdrawal: the Champa page does not mention the invasion, so confidence 1 stays. (5) The Emperor Xiaowu page is silent on the south and the Tuyuhun front; they remain unverified.
